children.text: Nowadays, work is no longer tied to an office space - people can work from almost anywhere. That's why many have decided to work from different corners of the world. Such people are called "Digital Nomads."

Unlike other remote workers, digital nomads often change locations to frequently switch environments, experience new cultures and people, and find their ideal workspace. Unfortunately, though, not every worker can become a nomad. As the name suggests, you've probably guessed that these people are employed in digital technology fields, which allows them to work remotely. They're mainly: digital marketers, developers, designers, and online business owners.

First, probably the most enjoyable benefit is the compatibility of work and travel. While other people spend the year preparing for travel, digital nomads travel and work simultaneously. Another big advantage is a flexible work schedule, allowing more time to be devoted to other important matters. Digital nomads typically build a very large network of contacts gathered through travel and online, which allows them to constantly have new opportunities coming their way.

page.title: What Are the Advantages of a Nomadic Lifestyle?

children.text: Probably the most important thing for this type of worker is reliable, high-quality internet and relatively affordable living conditions. For nomads from developed countries, it's also very important to keep their travel documents in order and generally stay organized, since they need to combine travel and work. Some people may feel lonely, since they can't establish connections in a new location. However, nomads typically choose locations where many of them gather together.

page.title: What Are the Challenges of Being a Digital Nomad?

children.text: As we already mentioned, affordable living conditions are very important, so countries where rent, taxes, and food are relatively cheap are the most popular locations. Such countries include: Portugal, Thailand, Mexico, Colombia, Hungary, and also Georgia. However, Portugal is the most popular, as it represents a complete combination of European quality of life, low prices, and good nature/weather.
If you think this lifestyle is right for you, feel free to reach out, and we'll help you handle all the bureaucracy related to your travel.
